title: Finite exact-couple boundaries as initial g-images of iterated alpha kernels
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category and $X$ a type-zero bigraded exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple]. Write $T$ for its canonical cycle-boundary tower, $\alpha^r_{p,q}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-r,q+r}$ for its outgoing alpha iterate, and $g_{p,q}:D^{p,q}\to E^{p,q}$ for its transported initial g [def-sp-convergence]. For every $r\in\mathbb N$ and $p,q\in\mathbb Z$, $T.B_r(p,q)=g_{p,q}(\ker\alpha^r_{p,q})$ as subobjects of $E^{p,q}$. No diagonal cocone or tail assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 011T, finite boundary formula; Tag 0AMJ, shifted exact-couple boundary formula

proof.text: Induct on r. At zero alphaIter is invertible and both boundary subobjects are zero. At a successor, use the canonical derived-D mono inclusions and iterated image epimorphisms. Their composite is alphaIter r; the derived alpha restriction gives the next iterate, and the derived g restriction identifies its image with the projected initial g. The projection and cycle-lift recurrences establish these identities by induction.

Exactness identifies the incoming differential image with derived g of the derived alpha kernel. Lift a successor-boundary representative through this image and then through the iterated image epimorphism, after epimorphic refinement. Its lift is killed by alphaIter(r+1). Subtract its initial g-image: the difference has zero projection, lies in the old boundary, and by induction is the initial g-image of a lift killed by alphaIter r. Add the lifts. Conversely a lift killed by alphaIter(r+1) maps into the derived alpha kernel, hence into an incoming differential boundary under derived g. Its initial g-image belongs to the successor pullback. Factorization descends along epimorphisms because a subobject is the kernel of its cokernel. These inclusions prove the equality.

theorem finiteBoundary_alphaKernel
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (X : BigradedExactCouple C 0) (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ) :
    X.cycleBoundaryTower.B r p q =
      (Subobject.«exists» (X.initialG p q)).obj (kernelSubobject (X.alphaIter r p q))
